nodes.name: Great Basin bristlecone pine
nodes.desc: Grows in open stands near treeline on rocky, often dolomite soils where few other plants thrive. It is the oldest known living non-clonal organism.

nodes.name: Limber pine
nodes.desc: A high-elevation pine whose large seeds are among the favourite foods of Clark's nutcracker.

nodes.name: Quaking aspen
nodes.desc: Forms groves on the wetter mountain slopes. Elk and mule deer browse it.

nodes.name: Curl-leaf mountain-mahogany
nodes.desc: A tough evergreen shrub of dry slopes that mule deer browse, especially in winter.

nodes.name: Big sagebrush
nodes.desc: Dominates the valley floors and lower slopes near the park and is key winter browse for mule deer.

nodes.name: Mountain meadow grasses & wildflowers
nodes.desc: Grasses and flowering plants of the wetter high meadows, eaten by elk, deer and small rodents.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: Mostly a browser, taking shrubs such as sagebrush, mountain-mahogany and aspen, with more flowering plants in summer. A main prey of cougars and coyotes.

nodes.name: Elk
nodes.desc: A large grazer and browser of the high slopes and meadows, and big prey for cougars.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: The most recorded small mammal near the park. Eats seeds and insects and is food for snakes, bobcats and coyotes.

nodes.name: Golden-mantled ground squirrel
nodes.desc: Eats seeds, plants and fungi in mountain forests and meadows, and is prey for eagles and carnivores.

nodes.name: Uinta chipmunk
nodes.desc: A conifer-forest chipmunk that eats seeds and other plant foods and is taken by bobcats and coyotes.

nodes.name: Clark's nutcracker
nodes.desc: Eats pine seeds and buries thousands for later; forgotten caches can sprout into new trees. Limber pine is among its important foods.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A very well recorded park bird and an opportunist that scavenges carcasses and takes snakes.

nodes.name: Gopher snake (bullsnake)
nodes.desc: A constrictor that hunts rodents such as mice and voles on valley and slope habitats.

nodes.name: Bobcat
nodes.desc: A park predator of rabbits, rodents, birds and young deer on the rugged slopes.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: Hunts rodents and takes fawns, and feeds on carcasses, across the park's valleys and slopes.

nodes.name: Cougar
nodes.desc: The top predator of the mountains. Across North America deer and elk are its main prey.

nodes.name: Golden eagle
nodes.desc: Hunts rabbits, hares and ground squirrels in open western country. Listed among the park's raptors.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Bright high-desert sun powers growth from the sagebrush valleys to the alpine slopes.

nodes.name: Snowpack & meltwater
nodes.desc: The mountains collect snow that feeds streams, springs and meadows in dry surroundings; the park even holds a small glacier.

nodes.name: Rocky mountain soils
nodes.desc: Thin, rocky and often limestone-based soils; bristlecone pines dominate dolomite ground where few other plants grow.

nodes.name: Fungi, bacteria & soil invertebrates
nodes.desc: Break down dead needles, plants and carcasses and return nutrients to the thin mountain soil.
